note.text: Distribution means whole-class coverage. A distributes S; E both; I neither; O P. Explain each using what the proposition covers. Do not confuse distribution with sample size or reverse an A claim without justification.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to state and justify which terms are distributed in each categorical form. Builds on: the A, E, I and O forms. Leads to: interpreting diagrams and avoiding illicit class-wide conclusions in later syllogisms.

sections.heading: What distributed means
sections.text: A term is distributed when the proposition speaks about every member of the class it names. This concerns logical coverage, not how many objects a classroom sample contains. Ask separately about S and P. A: S only. E: both. I: neither. O: P only. Learn the pattern with its reason, rather than treating a quantifier as a signal that both terms are distributed.

sections.heading: Why the affirmative forms differ
sections.text: All club members are badge holders covers every club member. It leaves open whether other badge holders exist, so P is undistributed. Some club members are badge holders covers selected members and does not exhaust either class. Thus A distributes S, while I distributes neither. Reversing an A statement would add a claim about the entire predicate class that the original did not make.

sections.heading: Why negative predicates are distributed
sections.text: No S are P excludes every S from the whole P class, so both terms are distributed. Some S are not P selects at least one S and excludes that member from P as a whole: S is undistributed, P distributed. The claim does not assert that all S are outside P. Distribution will later help test whether a conclusion claims more class coverage than its premises supply.

key_words.meaning: covering every member of the term’s class
not covering every member of the term’s class
whether P is covered as a whole

mistake.wrong: All S are P distributes both terms.
mistake.why: The statement permits P outside S, so it does not exhaust P.

worked_example.problem: Find the distributed terms in Some library books are not loanable items.
steps: Some selects at least one book, not every library book: S is undistributed.
That selected book is excluded from the entire loanable-item class: P is distributed.

cards.idea: Use class coverage for each term.
example: A: S only; E: both; I: neither; O: P only.

cards.idea: All covers every subject member, without exhausting the predicate.
example: All club members are badge holders still permits badge holders outside the club.

cards.idea: In O, the selected S is outside the whole P class.
example: Some S are not P: S undistributed, P distributed.

pick.r: The original A statement does not cover every member of the predicate class.
w: The original has no subject class.
All always means some but not all.
The original is necessarily an O statement.

All covers the whole subject, not merely a selection.
All S are P is A, not O.
pick.y: The predicate is undistributed in A; other P may lie outside S.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect claim, then read the reason for the correction.

right.explain: This is a correct rule: A distributes its subject only. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.
This is a correct rule: E distributes both terms. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.
This is a correct rule: I distributes neither term. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.
This is a correct rule: O distributes its predicate only. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

wrong.text: Distribution is the number of letters in a term.
wrong.explain: It concerns whole-class coverage, not spelling.

wrong.text: Some S are P distributes its subject because some is a quantifier.
wrong.explain: Some does not cover all S; I distributes neither term.

wrong.text: All S are P distributes P because every P must be S.
wrong.explain: A includes every S in P but allows other P.

wrong.text: A negative proposition never distributes its predicate.
wrong.explain: Both E and O distribute their predicate class.
